newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds outshone again by N.Z..
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds outshone again by N.Z..

text.p: Australian bonds proved the underperformer within the dollar bloc as the market contined to find the upside a difficult task given that an expected monetary policy easing had been fully discounted, traders said.

New Zealand debt again proved the market of the moment, building on Monday's strong post-election rally after its September quarter headline CPI rose a smaller than expected 0.6 percent, as did the underlying rate at 0.3 percent.
"As a result, the issues looking ahead are how much inflation will fall and when monetary policy easing will occur," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.
"Both issues are very positive issues for the bond market and should allow New Zealand long bond yields to test 7.5 percent in the relatively near term," he added.
New Zealand's 10-year premium over Australia shrank by double figures again to around 14 basis points having ended at some 50 basis points last Friday.

However, the N.Z. dollar was under pressure from the possibility of a policy easing in the future and after comments by Winston Peters, leader of the NZ First party which will hold the balance of power in a yet to be formed N.Z. coalition government.
Peter's said he thought the N.Z. dollar was overvalued for exporters and that it was not necessarily bad if talks with the major parties to form a government took until Christmas to resolve.

Meanwhile, the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread widened back above 100 basis points in relatively thin turnover as the market awaited Wednesday's Reserve Bank quarterly Bulletin for hints on monetary policy and the economy.
It is also awaiting the U.S. bond market to get back into full swing after Monday's Columbus Day holiday.
